newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-GROBBELAAR IS GREAT KEEPER, SAYS SCOTLAND'S WILSON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GROBBELAAR IS GREAT KEEPER, SAYS SCOTLAND'S WILSON.

text.p: Former Scottish goalkeeper Bob Wilson defended Bruce Grobbelaar on Tuesday, saying he was a great keeper and not at fault for a number of goals at the centre of a match-fixing trial.
Wilson told a court in this southern English town that the range of Grobbelaar's keeping when he played with Liverpool was the outstanding aspect of his game.

Asked after viewing videotape recordings of a number of games if he had seen anything untoward in Grobbelaar's play or positioning, Wilson replied: "Nothing untoward in any aspect of the games that I have viewed."
"The slightest hint he's behaved improperly or suspiciously?" he was asked by defence counsel Rodney Klevan.

Grobbelaar is accused with former Wimbledon keeper Hans Segers, ex-Wimbledon and Aston Villa striker John Fashanu and Malaysian businessman Heng Suan Lim of rigging games to benefit an Asian betting syndicate.
All four defendants deny the charges although both keepers admit they were paid in cash by Lim for providing match forecasts.
Wilson, a former Arsenal goalkeeper and now a top sports commentator, praised Zimbabwean-born Grobbelaar as an unorthodox star who was prepared to leave the penalty area and act as an extra defender.
"The problem with it was, when he got the decision wrong, they were spectacularly wrong and he was yards away from his charge, which was the goal."
Wilson told the court he had devoted a chapter to Grobbelaar in his book on goalkeepers entitled: "You have got to be crazy."
"I felt it was necessary to include Bruce. He was still at Liverpool at the time but such was his impression on me and other goalkeepers.
"If there is one football club where you are not allowed to be anything other than truly consistent, it is Liverpool Football Club," he told the court.
During his 13 years at Liverpool, Grobbelaar won five league titles and became English club soccer's most successful goalkeeper. He now plays for second division Plymouth.

Asked about Liverpool's 3-0 defeat at Newcastle United in November 1993, which Grobbelaar is alleged to have thrown, Wilson said Grobbelaar had no chance of saving any of the goals, and made a truly outstanding save very low to his right.
The next match, viewed on video tape in court, was Liverpool's 3-3 draw with Manchester United in January 1994.
Wilson said Grobbelaar made two saves "which any fellow professional would look at and admire and wish that he could have made as great a save".

Wilson told the jury that one save during the game was the "most perfect example" of being in the right place and position. Another save was typical of Grobbelaar as he showed great agility to get down to the ball, he said.
